body.justification: This sanity reduction prevents spurious absorption bias when heterogeneous treatment variation is absent.
body.gap: Bai (2009) supplies the homogeneous-effect benchmark but not its embedding as the zero-signal point of a local profile.
body.consumer: The theoretical sensitivity map reduces to the familiar homogeneous-effect benchmark at zero amplitude.
body.proof_tex:
At \(\theta=0\), the noise-scale bound implies \(h=0\), while the definition of the causal target gives \(\operatorname{ATT}_{NT}=\gamma\).  Moreover,
\[
B_{\eta,0}(x)=-\kappa x e_{11},\qquad
s_1\{B_{\eta,0}(x)\}=\kappa|x|.                               \tag{30}
\]
If \(\kappa|x|\leq c^{1/4}\), then
\[
\Phi_{\eta,0}(x)=\kappa^2x^2-(1+\sqrt c)^2,
\]
which is uniquely minimized at zero.  If \(\kappa|x|>c^{1/4}\), then
\[
\Phi_{\eta,0}(x)=-(1+c)-\frac{c}{\kappa^2x^2}
>-(1+c)-\sqrt c
>-(1+c)-2\sqrt c=\Phi_{\eta,0}(0).                             \tag{31}
\]
Thus \(\mathcal S(\eta,0)=\{0\}\), with strict global separation.  Applying \(\mathrm{thm{:}uniform\mbox{-}profile}\) yields \(\widehat x_F\to_p0\), equivalently \(\sqrt m(\widehat\beta_F-\gamma)/\sigma\to_p0\).  Together with \(\operatorname{ATT}_{NT}=\gamma\), this proves every assertion.
